We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume buyable). Need to construct route using templates.

We have some buyable building blocks: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride), Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-phenylenediamine?), actually that's aniline with amine at para? SMILES: Nc1ccc(N)cc1 is p-phenylenediamine (two amines). Also C=CC(=O)Cl (acryloyl chloride). Also C=CC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (acrylamide with aniline). Also Cc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-toluidine) is buyable? Not checked but likely.

Goal: target is a sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So we can think retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide bond: target -> sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline derivative (the rest). So we need to form sulfonamide via reaction of sulfonyl chloride with amine.

Thus precursor A: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) (buyable). Precursor B: the amine part: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (a phenyl ring with para substituent of the unsaturated amide). This is an aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached to the unsaturated amide. So B is 4-(E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Actually structure: phenyl ring with para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). The phenyl ring has an amine at para position (since NS(=O)... attaches to that amine). So B is 4-aminophenyl with the unsaturated amide attached at para? Wait the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This phenyl has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N at para position relative to the sulfonamide attachment point (which is the amine). So B is 4-(E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Actually the amide attaches to phenyl c3ccccc3N (an aniline). So the amide is attached to an aniline (anilide). So B is 4-[(E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamido]aniline? Wait there are two aniline groups: one on the phenyl ring (the sulfonamide amine) and one on the amide side (Nc3ccccc3N). So B is a diamino phenyl with unsaturated amide linking to another aniline.

Thus we can further disconnect the amide bond: the amide formed from a carboxylic acid derivative (acryloyl chloride) reacting with aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So we can have precursor C: C=CC(=O)Cl (acryloyl chloride) (buyable) and precursor D: Nc3ccccc3N (p-phenylenediamine? Actually that's aniline with an extra amine? Wait Nc3ccccc3N is aniline with an amine at para? That's p-phenylenediamine again. But the SMILES shows an aniline with an amine at para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is aniline with an amine at both positions? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N => two amines at positions 1 and 6? That's p-phenylenediamine again. So the amide attaches to one of the amines, leaving the other free for sulfonamide later. So we could use p-phenylenediamine as the core, but we need two phenyl rings: one is the tolyl sulfonyl chloride attached to one amine, the other amine forms amide with acryloyl chloride, then the amide attaches to the other phenyl? Wait the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) which is a phenyl with an amine. That amine is used to form the amide, leaving the other amine free for later? Actually the amide is formed with the nitrogen attached to carbonyl: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So the nitrogen of the amide is attached to the phenyl ring (aniline). That nitrogen is part of the amide, not the free amine. The phenyl ring also has another amine (the one that will become sulfonamide). So indeed p-phenylenediamine is the central scaffold.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> sulfonyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine with acryloyl attached? Wait we need to incorporate the unsaturated chain.

Better route:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and p-phenylenediamine (one amine). This yields intermediate I: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Actually after reaction we get sulfonamide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1 attached to p-phenylenediamine? Wait the sulfonyl chloride reacts with an amine to give sulfonamide, releasing HCl. So product is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1 attached to the amine of p-phenylenediamine, giving a molecule where the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring of tolyl and the nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring of p-phenylenediamine. So intermediate I is exactly the target but missing the acryloyl amide on the other amine. So we need to acylate the second amine with acryloyl chloride to give the unsaturated amide. So step 2: acylation of the remaining amine with acryloyl chloride (C=CC(=O)Cl) to give final product.

Thus only 2 steps.

Leaves: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (buyable), p-phenylenediamine (buyable), acryloyl chloride (buyable). All are commercially available.

We need to provide route JSON with reactions and template IDs. Need to find appropriate template IDs for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine) and amide formation (acyl chloride + amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates.

Let's search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_broken: primary amines? Actually reaction forms sulfonamide from sulfonyl chloride and amine, breaking H-Cl bond? Not sure. Use functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides. Let's search.
